title: Big Fish
events_chronological: As a boy in Ashton, Edward Bloom looks into the eye of the witch in the swamp and sees how he will die, and so knows he will survive everything before it.
Edward grows into the town's champion at everything and saves Ashton from the giant Karl by befriending him.
Edward and Karl leave Ashton together and part at a fork in the road, Edward taking the hard path through the woods.
Edward stumbles into the hidden town of Spectre, where nobody wears shoes and nobody ever leaves, and meets a little girl called Jenny.
Edward leaves Spectre anyway and joins Amos Calloway's circus, working three years unpaid for one fact a month about a girl he glimpsed across the tent.
Edward learns the girl is Sandra Templeton, fills a field with daffodils for her, and takes a beating from her fiance Don Price.
Edward marries Sandra and is drafted to Korea, where he steals secret papers and is carried home by the conjoined singers Ping and Jing.
Reported dead, Edward walks back into Sandra's life, and Don Price drops dead of a heart attack.
Edward becomes a travelling salesman away from home for weeks at a time and robs a bank with the poet Norther Winslow.
Edward tells his tall tales at his son Will's birth and at every family occasion afterwards.
Edward hijacks Will's wedding reception with the story of catching the uncatchable catfish using his own wedding ring as bait.
Humiliated, Will stops speaking to his father for three years.
Edward goes back to Spectre, finds it derelict and repossessed, buys the town to save it, and meets the grown Jenny.
Will, living in Paris with his pregnant wife Josephine, is told by his mother that Edward is dying.
Will comes home and tries to get one true story out of his father, who will only tell the same tales.
Will finds the deed to Spectre among the papers and drives out to meet Jenny, who tells him the truth: Edward never left Sandra.
Edward has a stroke, and from his hospital bed he asks Will to tell him how he dies.
Will invents an ending in which he carries his father to the river and Edward turns into a great fish and swims away, and Edward dies happy.
At the funeral every character from the stories turns up, ordinary and real, and Will sees how much of it was true after all.
Will tells the same stories to his own small son by the river.
syuzhet_notes: The frame is Will's return to his dying father. Told-order bullets 1-3 are a prologue of childhood and wedding-day memories, and bullets 6-14 are Edward's tall tales, flashbacks he narrates and the film stages at face value with no marker that they are unreliable. Bullet 15 is a flashback Will assembles from documents rather than from his father, and the last five bullets return to the present.
fabula_notes: Most of the flashbacks are Edward's embroidered version rather than what happened, and the film shows them as told; the funeral is what reveals which characters were real. The salesman years are compressed into a montage, and Edward's decline happens between Will's visits.
